item.title: Pakistan ranks lowest in South Asia on hunger index amid rising food prices
item.description: Pakistan's 2026 Global Hunger Index standings reveal an alarming crisis, showcasing the worst performance in South Asia amid ongoing economic challenges. Soaring food prices and the increasing frequency of climate-related disasters have sharply intensified food insecurity. With around 218 million individuals in South Asia experiencing undernourishment from 2023 to 2025, urgent strategies are required to bolster access to healthy food and enhance agricultural resilience against severe weather patterns. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A fungus is threatening the world’s food supply. Scientists just found a new defense
item.description: Scientists have discovered a potential new weapon against a devastating fungus that threatens rice, wheat, and barley worldwide. By engineering a special type of plant immune receptor, researchers created defenses capable of recognizing multiple fungal threats at once. The breakthrough could eventually lead to crops with powerful, long-lasting disease resistance, helping protect a global food supply increasingly threatened by spreading infections and climate change. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Mont Blanc nearly two metres taller than in 2023
item.description: France's tallest mountain was nearly two metres higher last month than its last reported measurement in 2023, surveyors said Wednesday, putting the Alpine peak at 4,807.47 metres (15,772.5 feet). item.title: Countries most vulnerable to fossil fuel phaseout generate just 6% of global output, climate analysis finds
item.description: Countries highly vulnerable to the phase-out of oil, gas and coal account for just 6% of global economic output, countries in Africa stand to benefit from their vast solar energy potential, and the economic interests of the U.S., Europe and China are affected by climate policy in surprisingly similar ways. A study by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) published in Nature Sustainability now shows, for 169 countries around the world, how the fight against global heating affects national assets—and what geopolitical challenges and opportunities arise as a result. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 38 mil reproducciones · 177 reacciones | Durante defesa de cliente - O advogado Airton Jacob Gonçalves Graton acendeu um cigarro e fumou durante uma sustentação oral por videoconferência enquanto pedia a concessão de prisão domiciliar para um cliente, que foi negado posteriormente, na 3ª Câmara Criminal do Tribunal de Justiça de Mato Grosso (TJMT), nesta quarta-feira (14). ➡️ O g1 tenta localizar o advogado citado. Imagens da sessão, transmitida ao vivo pelo YouTube, mostram o momento em que o advogado aparece diante da câmera, durante sua manifestação aos magistrados. Enquanto apresenta os argumentos em defesa do cliente, ele acende o cigarro e começa a fumar, sem interromper a sustentação oral. A cena ocorre durante a sessão virtual, acompanhada pelos integrantes da Câmara Criminal. Antes de iniciar a defesa, Graton também pediu desculpas por não estar usando beca, vestimenta tradicionalmente utilizada por advogados em julgamentos perante os tribunais. O relator do caso, desembargador Gilberto Giraldelli, recebeu a justificativa de forma cortês. O pedido de prisão domiciliar foi rejeitado por unanimidade. Os desembargadores Paulo Sérgio Carreira de Sousa e Agamenon Alcântara acompanharam o voto do relator. A Resolução nº 354/2020 do Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ), que regulamenta audiências e sessões por videoconferência e telepresenciais, estabelece, no artigo 7º, inciso VI, que os participantes devem observar a mesma liturgia dos atos processuais presenciais, inclusive em relação às vestimentas.
